content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The text adjudicates a collision in which each Isaiah 7:14 link is pressed by the other side's own chain read together (CR2's 7:13-14/8:3/8:8/9:6-7 row against DR3's 7:14/7:16/8:3-4/8:8 row), the exact situation K-C governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D3 vs C6 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] answered the Isaiah 8:3-4 bound with 8:8 and 9:6-7, while [DR3] presses the sign's own bounds; the sign itself does not state the mechanism.", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "Phrase: 'never verse by verse' together with 'the stating-verse test DG-61 retires.' Reading 1: the final clause merely reports why the sign alone cannot settle the matter, with the UNDERDETERMINED resting on an unspoken balance of the two chains' footing. Reading 2: the final clause is the operative ground -- the judge let one verse's own silence (the sign not stating the mechanism) yield the verdict. I weighed Reading 2 because the judge wrote no footing comparison and rested the verdict on the sign's own non-statement.", "why": "Facing a chain-against-chain collision the judge decided by what one verse itself does not state, which is the very stating-verse test K-C retires at a judge's seat, instead of weighing the two chains' footing against each other."}
